thread:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: multiple serving pods in us-west-2 hit OOMs over the last 18m. Autoscale kicked but nodes kept flapping. Root hint: paged-attention allocator showing high fragmentation + KV cache resident set growth (slow).

oncall-alex: seeing the same from the metrics dashboard. 3 pods bounced in the past 12m, one container crash with CUDA error 700 (out of memory).

sre-maya: I’m attaching recent excerpt from dmesg and container logs — looks like repeated allocation failures during attention paging.

runtime-jon: can you paste the allocator stack trace? I want to confirm whether it's slab fragmentation or page-reservation failure.

sre-maya: logs snippet:

```
[2026-03-17T02:12:34Z] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-17T02:12:34Z] paged_allocator: page_alloc(128M) -> ENOMEM
[2026-03-17T02:12:34Z] kv_cache: resident_bytes+=48M (pinned)
```

runtime-jon: thanks. Sounds like small repeated page requests are creating micro-fragmentation. The KV cache warmup plus attention paging is causing non-contiguous free pages.

eng-ml-rita: workload note — we rolled out model v3.2.1 to canary yesterday which increased typical context length. Might increase KV cache pressure.

oncall-alex: customer impact check — cs-lina, any reports?

cs-lina: two customers reported degraded latency and 429s for heavy batching flows; both on Dedicated pools in us-west-2. I opened support tickets.

platform-lee: creating a temp routing rule to move new requests to us-east-1 for affected tiers (canary & prod-burst). Will patch route in 30s. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: Routing update deployed to edge: redirecting 7% of traffic from us-west-2 -> us-east-1 for model v3.2.1.

runtime-jon: mitigation proposals:
- force-evict small KV entries older than 3h (reduce resident by ~15-20%)
- reduce max batch size to limit attention window growth
- enable aggressive page compaction on affected nodes (experimental)

oncall-alex: can we apply force-evict and batch cap immediately? Which is safest?

eng-ml-rita: force-evict OK for non-active prefixes, we need a quick check to avoid harming low-latency sessions. I can mark pinned prefixes.

runtime-jon: I’ll push a conservative eviction: `kv_cache.evict(age>10800 && not pinned)` on the cluster. Also lowering max_batch_tokens to 1024 for v3.2.1 routes.

sre-maya: executed eviction command on 3 nodes (pod ids: rwi-117, rwi-119, rwi-123). Resident went down ~22% on those. Memory headroom improved but fragmentation still visible.

noncall-alex: any CUDA errors after eviction?

sre-maya: one container still crashed after compaction attempt, got CUDA error 702 -> device-side assert. Restarted and it came up. No further OOMs in the last 6m on those nodes.

cs-lina: customers seeing partial recovery (latency back to normal for 1 of 2 affected). I'll update tickets and ask for any remaining logs.

platform-lee: enabling page compaction daemon in experimental mode on remaining nodes. It runs background compaction which may cause temporary CPU jitter. Approved for five nodes.

runtime-jon: note: compaction is best-effort; if fragmentation is due to kernel selection for attention, compaction may not recover all holes. We should consider temporary model downgrade to v3.1.x for sessions that require long context until we fix allocator.

eng-ml-rita: canary rollback to v3.1.x is available; we can route v3.2.1 -> v3.1 for affected capacity. That will reduce context memory by ~30% per session.

noncall-alex: do it. Platform-lee, please route traffic for v3.2.1 -> v3.1 for the dedicated pools in us-west-2.

platform-lee: routing change applied. Traffic shifting now (5% per minute), monitoring closely.

deploy-bot: Route update: 100% of v3.2.1 in us-west-2 now fallback to v3.1.

sre-maya: after fallback and eviction, node headroom stable; no new OOMs in last 10m. Fragmentation metrics (free contiguous page runs) improved by ~18% post-compaction.

runtime-jon: next steps (short):
- repro on staging with long-context workloads and KV warmup to validate allocator fixes
- add guardrails: automatic KV eviction policy when fragmentation > threshold
- longer term: allocator redesign to reduce page churn for paged-attention kernel

eng-ml-rita: I’ll coordinate a canary of allocator patch in staging tomorrow morning and run our long-context perf suite.

cs-lina: I’ll follow up with customers and share timeline for fix + mitigation steps.

oncall-alex: thanks all — keeping this as a live SEV2 until we have patch + staged validation. Will update every 30m. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident SEV2 acknowledged. This thread will be archived when the incident is resolved.
